# mdwire

> Send LLM-generated Markdown to chat channels without it breaking. mdwire does not render Markdown into finished output; it tailors the Markdown an agent wrote to each channel: it repairs it, rewrites it into the syntax each channel accepts, and splits it within the channel's length limit, in one shot or while tokens stream in.

Pipeline: normalize → render for channel → split safely → send.

Channels (the name each API takes):

- `telegram-html` — Telegram `parse_mode: "HTML"` (nine tags, 4096-character limit)
- `slack-markdown` — Slack `markdown_text` (standard Markdown, 12,000)
- `github-markdown` — GitHub comments, GFM (65,536); a `~` or `<` meant as a character is escaped
- `notion-markdown` — Notion page body, Notion-flavored Markdown (65,536); inline HTML Notion cannot draw is stripped
- `plain` — plain text
- `html` — HTML for the browser, safe to set as `innerHTML`: text is escaped and, by default, only `http(s)`/`mailto` links become `<a>` (line breaks, images and allowed schemes are options)

Use mdwire when:

- a bot or agent posts model output to Telegram, Slack, GitHub or Notion — instead of a regex converter or escaping everything by hand
- Telegram answers `Bad Request: can't parse entities` for an LLM answer (unclosed `**` or code fence, an unescaped `<`)
- a streamed answer shows stray `**` or half-drawn formatting, or a Telegram message passes 4,096 characters and must be split without cutting through a tag
- streaming LLM Markdown into React without `innerHTML`
- Korean (or other CJK) text puts a particle right after bold (`**52%**다`), which CommonMark renderers leave unclosed

Things that are easy to get wrong:

- Streaming is append-only: what `push` returns is final and `finish` only appends the tail, so the pieces concatenated equal a one-shot `render` (unless the document is long enough to be split into parts).
- A channel that rewrites the whole message (Telegram edit) sends the accumulated output plus `preview()`. An append-only channel (Slack `appendStream`) sends each `push` piece as is and never calls `preview()`.
- The repair report counts what the normalizer fixed: closed emphasis, closed code fences, backtick runs kept as text, dropped `**` — and what the channel rewrote: escapes, tag emphasis, stripped HTML, bullets, tables, converted markers.
- One Rust core with no dependencies. The CLI, the npm package (WASM) and the Go implementation are held to the same test cases.
- `SPEC.md` and `DESIGN.md` are written in Korean.

## Docs

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/minjun0219/mdwire/main/README.md): install and usage for the CLI, Rust, npm, React and Go
- [README (Korean)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/minjun0219/mdwire/main/README.ko.md): the same in Korean
- [SPEC](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/minjun0219/mdwire/main/SPEC.md): what v0.1 covers and what was deliberately deferred (Korean)
- [DESIGN](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/minjun0219/mdwire/main/DESIGN.md): the measurements behind each decision (Korean)

## For agents

- [Agent skill](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/minjun0219/mdwire/main/skills/mdwire/SKILL.md): when to use mdwire, which channel and entry point to pick, and copyable code for each language (Agent Skills format). In Claude Code: `/plugin marketplace add minjun0219/mdwire`, then `/plugin install mdwire@mdwire`
- WebMCP: pages on this site register a `mdwire_render` tool (`markdown`, `channel`, optional `limit`) that runs mdwire in the page and returns the parts and the repair report

## Packages

- [npm `@minjun0219/mdwire`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@minjun0219/mdwire): `render`, `renderWithReport`, `Streamer`; `@minjun0219/mdwire/react` (`Markdown`, `useMarkdownStream`), `@minjun0219/mdwire/events`, and `@minjun0219/mdwire/lezer` (`koreanEmphasis`, a `@lezer/markdown` extension that reads emphasis the way mdwire does)
- [crates.io `mdwire-core`](https://crates.io/crates/mdwire-core): the Rust library, imported as `mdwire`
- [crates.io `mdwire-cli`](https://crates.io/crates/mdwire-cli): the `mdwire` command — `mdwire --channel <name> [--stream] [--report]`
- [Go `github.com/minjun0219/mdwire/go`](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/minjun0219/mdwire/go): the Go implementation, library and CLI

## Site

Docs pages are Markdown at the page path plus `.md` (`/docs/npm/` → `/docs/npm.md`, `/ko/docs/` → `/ko/docs.md`).

- [Overview](https://minjun.kim/mdwire/index.md): what mdwire does
- [Why another one](https://minjun.kim/mdwire/why.md): three gaps in existing tools (emphasis across lines, Korean notation, streaming)
- [Cases](https://minjun.kim/mdwire/why/cases.md): real failures (emphasis across lines, bold before a Korean particle, tildes, masked numbers, unclosed fences, Korean tables, splitting) and what mdwire sends instead
- [Demos](https://minjun.kim/mdwire/demo/), all in the browser: [Telegram vs. Slack](https://minjun.kim/mdwire/demo/channels/) (one agent answer converted for both), [Streaming](https://minjun.kim/mdwire/demo/streaming/) (token by token into react-markdown, Streamdown, mdwire in front of Streamdown, and mdwire's React hook), [Before and after repair](https://minjun.kim/mdwire/demo/repair/) (broken agent output next to what mdwire sends, with the repair report)
- [Korean](https://minjun.kim/mdwire/ko/): the site in Korean
- [Docs: concepts](https://minjun.kim/mdwire/docs.md): channels, options, the repair report, the streaming contract
- [Docs: npm](https://minjun.kim/mdwire/docs/npm.md) · [Rust](https://minjun.kim/mdwire/docs/rust.md) · [Go](https://minjun.kim/mdwire/docs/go.md) · [CLI](https://minjun.kim/mdwire/docs/cli.md): the API of each
- [Docs: emphasis before Korean particles](https://minjun.kim/mdwire/docs/emphasis.md): why CommonMark parsers leave `**설정(config)**을` unclosed, the reading rule mdwire uses, and what GitHub, Slack and Notion need on output
- [Full docs](https://minjun.kim/mdwire/llms-full.txt): the overview, why, cases and every docs page above in one file
